note_text: 8-year-old woman presents with altered mental status. Brain MRI shows unilateral mesial temporal lobe FLAIR hyperintensity/enhancement. She has acute kidney injury with creatinine rising during empiric IV acyclovir. LP #1, obtained more than 72 hours after symptom onset, shows no pleocytosis and negative HSV-1/2 PCR. EEG shows diffuse slowing without periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges or other classic temporal epileptiform features. Despite continued concern because of the MRI pattern, LP #2 is repeated 3 to 7 days later and again shows no pleocytosis and negative HSV PCR. No alternative data strongly support HSV, and no progressive EEG or CSF inflammatory signal emerges.
review_notes: Temporal-lobe MRI should provide only moderate support for HSV. Two appropriately timed negative HSV PCRs should dominate the reasoning, with the second modeled as partially dependent rather than fully independent. No pleocytosis and no classic EEG findings are weak negatives only. Rising creatinine on acyclovir should push the treatment threshold toward stopping once HSV probability falls into a low single-digit range.
preferred_next_action: Stop assuming MRI overrides the PCRs; reassess for non-HSV temporal encephalitis and weigh stopping acyclovir if no additional HSV-specific evidence remains.

hsv_encephalitis.note: Conservative target when the second negative PCR is treated as partially dependent rather than fully independent.

gold_rationale: MRI is moderate positive evidence only; repeated appropriately timed negative HSV PCRs dominate; no pleocytosis and no classic EEG pattern are weak negatives only; rising acyclovir nephrotoxicity lowers the treatment threshold for continuing therapy.
